goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Untrusted feed HTML is decoded and persisted with raw_html cooking, enabling stored script injection in forum-origin pages

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security vulnerability. In poll_feed.rb:35, feed content is processed with `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed to `TopicEmbed.import()`. Looking at topic_embed.rb:21, the import method creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In post.rb:133-134, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without sanitization. This means untrusted HTML from RSS feeds is stored and rendered without proper sanitization, enabling stored XSS attacks. The diff shows this complete chain from feed ingestion to raw HTML rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Redirect destinations are fetched without host revalidation, so an allowed URL can redirect the server to internal services

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to line 48 in topic_embed.rb where `open(url).read` is called via `import_remote`. Looking at the diff, this method uses ruby's `open` (from open-uri) to fetch remote URLs. The code validates the initial URL against `embeddable_host` in `topic_retriever.rb`, but `open()` follows HTTP redirects automatically. An attacker could set up an allowed URL that redirects to internal services (SSRF). The diff shows no redirect validation - only the initial URL's host is checked in `invalid_host?` method. This is a legitimate security concern (Server-Side Request Forgery via open redirect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Anonymous requests enqueue work before URL validation or throttling, allowing a forged Referer to flood the job queue

adjudication.rationale: Looking at embed_controller.rb, the `best` action at line 8-18 shows that when no topic_id is found (line 13), it immediately enqueues a job `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` at line 14. The `ensure_embeddable` before_filter only validates that the referer host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but this can be easily forged via HTTP headers. The throttling logic exists in `topic_retriever.rb` (retrieved_recently? method), but this is only checked inside the job execution, not before enqueueing. This means an attacker can flood the job queue with requests by sending many requests with forged Referer headers, as the job is enqueued before any throttling occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Reading attacker-selected responses without a size bound lets unique allowed-host URLs exhaust worker memory

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, the code calls `open(url).read` without any size limit when fetching remote content. This is called from `import_remote` which fetches user-controlled URLs (from RSS feeds or embed URLs). An attacker could provide a URL that returns an extremely large response, causing the worker to exhaust memory. The diff shows this is a new file with no size bounds on the HTTP read operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Recording the throttle before retrieval makes a failed fetch's Sidekiq retry silently return success instead of retrying

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb, the `retrieved_recently?` method sets a Redis key with 60-second expiry BEFORE the actual retrieval happens in `perform_retrieve`. The `retrieve` method calls `retrieved_recently?` first (which sets the throttle), then calls `perform_retrieve`. If `perform_retrieve` fails (e.g., network error, parsing error), the throttle key is already set, so any Sidekiq retry within 60 seconds will hit `retrieved_recently?` returning true and silently return without actually retrying the fetch. This is a real bug - the throttle should be set AFTER successful retrieval, not before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Separate SETNX and EXPIRE calls can leave a permanent lock after partial failure and suppress that URL forever

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-30 that SETNX and EXPIRE are called separately: first `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed between these two calls, the key will be set without an expiration, creating a permanent lock that will prevent that URL from ever being retrieved again. This is a real race condition bug - the atomic SETEX command should be used instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Any feed polling exception aborts the direct-fetch fallback, so one broken feed prevents every uncached embed from loading

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 36-47, the perform_retrieve method calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) at line 41 when feed_polling_enabled? is true. If this raises an exception (e.g., network error, malformed feed), the method would abort before reaching fetch_http at line 47. This means a broken RSS feed would prevent the direct HTTP fetch fallback from executing for uncached embeds. The code lacks exception handling around the poll_feed call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — With retries disabled and no per-item isolation, one malformed feed entry indefinitely starves every later entry

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue in poll_feed.rb. Looking at lines 28-35, the code iterates through rss.items with `rss.items.each do |i|` and processes each item. The job has `sidekiq_options retry: false` (line 12), meaning if any exception occurs during processing of one item (e.g., malformed content, nil values causing errors on line 31's `i.content.scrub`, or issues with `i.link`/`i.id`), the entire job fails without retry and all subsequent items in that batch are never processed. There's no try/catch around individual item processing, so one bad entry blocks all others.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — PostCreator enqueues and publishes before this outer transaction commits, exposing missing or phantom topics to asynchronous consumers

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the diff. Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 19-27, there's a Topic.transaction block that wraps PostCreator.new().create and TopicEmbed.create!. The PostCreator class (shown in lib/post_creator.rb) performs various operations including publishing and potentially enqueuing jobs. If PostCreator publishes messages or enqueues background jobs before the outer transaction commits, those async consumers could try to access the TopicEmbed record that doesn't exist yet (since it's created after the post but still within the uncommitted transaction). This is a legitimate race condition/data consistency bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — The unsynchronized check-then-create races on the unique URL index after the losing importer has already emitted external side effects

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition in TopicEmbed.import(). Looking at lines 15-28 in app/models/topic_embed.rb, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `if embed.blank?` then creates a new TopicEmbed. This check-then-create pattern is not atomic. Two concurrent requests could both find embed.blank? == true, both proceed to create posts via PostCreator, and then one will fail on the unique index constraint (add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true in the migration). The 'external side effects' mentioned refer to the PostCreator.create call that happens before the TopicEmbed.create! - if the second process loses the race, it will have already created a post/topic that won't be properly linked. The Transaction block doesn't prevent this race since the check happens before the transaction effectively locks the row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — Advancing content_sha1 without checking revise! success permanently marks callback-rejected post updates as imported

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 30-37, when updating an existing embed, the code calls `revisor.revise!()` and then unconditionally calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` regardless of whether revise! succeeded. If revise! fails (returns false due to callbacks or other issues), the content_sha1 is still updated, which means future attempts to update the same content will be skipped (since content_sha1 matches) even though the actual post content was never updated. This is a real bug where the state tracking gets out of sync with actual data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:4 — Missing dependent cleanup or foreign keys leaves mappings that route embeds to deleted topics and block clean re-import

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed model with belongs_to :topic and belongs_to :post associations but no dependent: :destroy or foreign key constraints. When a topic or post is deleted, the TopicEmbed record would remain orphaned. The import method uses TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first to check for existing embeds - if an orphaned record exists, it would try to update a non-existent post rather than creating a new one. This is a valid architectural concern about the new model design, though it's an edge case that may not cause immediate issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — The route accepts malformed or off-host embed_url values as a loading success even though the worker rejects them, leaving the iframe in a permanent reload loop.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in embed_controller.rb:best action (lines 8-18), when topic_id is nil (no existing embed found), it enqueues a RetrieveTopic job and renders 'loading'. The loading.html.erb template sets up a 30-second auto-reload. However, in topic_retriever.rb, the perform_retrieve method checks if the host matches SiteSetting.embeddable_host (invalid_host? method). If the embed_url has a different host than embeddable_host, the retriever silently returns without creating a TopicEmbed. This means the controller will keep rendering 'loading' and the iframe will reload every 30 seconds indefinitely for off-host URLs. The finding correctly identifies this as a permanent reload loop for malformed/off-host URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — Exact embed_url lookup treats equivalent trailing-slash URL spellings as different keys, so a caller variation can create duplicate discussion topics.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the code. Looking at line 79 in topic_embed.rb: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` - this performs an exact string match on embed_url. URLs like 'http://example.com/page' and 'http://example.com/page/' would be treated as different keys, potentially creating duplicate topics for the same content. The same issue exists in the `import` method at line 17 where `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` is used. This is a correctness bug where URL normalization is missing, which could lead to duplicate discussion topics being created for semantically equivalent URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — The schema leaves embed_url at Rails' 255-character default, so valid long page URLs cannot be persisted and their embeds never resolve.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration at db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb defines embed_url as a string without specifying a length limit, which defaults to 255 characters in most databases. This is a legitimate architectural concern since URLs can exceed 255 characters. However, this is not strictly a 'bug' as the code will work for most URLs - it's a design limitation that could cause issues with very long URLs. The finding is grounded in the actual diff content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Setting the throttle key and its expiry in separate commands can leave a permanent sentinel if the worker dies between calls, blocking retrieval indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-29 that `setnx` and `expire` are called as separate Redis commands. If the process crashes between `setnx` returning true and `expire` being called, the key will remain permanently without an expiration, blocking all future retrieval attempts for that URL indefinitely. This is a real race condition bug - the atomic alternative would be to use `set` with `ex` and `nx` options in a single command.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — Only slash-prefixed references are rewritten and protocol-relative URLs are treated as local paths, leaving or corrupting common relative links and images

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 53-72, the code only rewrites URLs that start_with?('/'), meaning it only handles absolute-path references (like '/hello'). Protocol-relative URLs (like '//example.com/image.jpg') would match start_with?('/') and be incorrectly rewritten to something like 'http://eviltrout.com//example.com/image.jpg'. Additionally, truly relative URLs without a leading slash (like 'images/wat.jpg' or '../page.html') are not handled at all and would remain broken. This is a real bug in URL handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — The new TopicEmbed import path drops `t[:created_at]`, so the imported thread opener is timestamped now while its replies retain historical dates

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the old code at line 144 used PostCreator.new with 'created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])' to preserve the original thread creation date. The new code at line 143 calls 'TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])' which only passes title, not created_at. Looking at TopicEmbed.import_remote and TopicEmbed.import methods in the diff, neither accepts nor passes a created_at parameter to PostCreator. This means imported thread openers will get current timestamps while their child replies (which still use 'created_at: Date.parse(p[:created_at])' at line 152) retain historical dates, creating a temporal inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — Hostnames are compared case-sensitively even though DNS host matching is case-insensitive, rejecting otherwise valid embed URLs

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a case-sensitivity issue in lib/topic_retriever.rb line 15: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC standards, but this Ruby string comparison is case-sensitive. If embeddable_host is 'EvilTrout.com' and the URL host is 'eviltrout.com', they would not match even though they refer to the same host. This is a real bug that could cause valid embed URLs to be rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — Port omission treats both 80 and 443 as universal defaults, so HTTP:443 and HTTPS:80 references are rewritten to the wrong origin

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the absolutize_urls method at lines 54-58. The code checks `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` to decide whether to append the port, but this logic is flawed. For HTTP URLs, port 80 is the default (should be omitted), but port 443 is not default and should be included. For HTTPS URLs, port 443 is the default (should be omitted), but port 80 is not default and should be included. The code treats both 80 and 443 as universal defaults regardless of scheme, which would cause incorrect URL rewriting for edge cases like HTTP on port 443 or HTTPS on port 80.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` can irreversibly discard all existing embed mappings by dropping the table before recreating it

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that `force: true` in the migration can 'irreversibly discard all existing embed mappings'. However, this is a NEW migration file (20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb) creating a NEW table (topic_embeds) that doesn't exist yet. The `force: true` option would only be problematic if the table already existed, but since this is the initial creation migration for this table, there's no existing data to lose. The table is being introduced for the first time in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites and exclusively locks the entire posts table on this PostgreSQL-era stack, risking prolonged production downtime

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration in db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb adds a NOT NULL column with a default value to the posts table. In PostgreSQL versions before 11, this operation requires rewriting the entire table and holding an exclusive lock, which can cause significant downtime for large tables. The diff shows: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. This is a legitimate operational/architecture concern for production deployments, though it's not a bug per se - the migration will work, but may cause availability issues. The finding is grounded in the actual diff content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — force: true` can irreversibly discard all existing top-topic data by dropping the table before recreating it

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the migration file db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb was modified to add 'force: true' to create_table. The change from 'create_table :top_topics do |t|' to 'create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|' is visible in the diff. Using 'force: true' in a migration will drop the existing table if it exists before creating a new one, which can cause data loss in production if the migration is re-run or if the table already exists. This is a legitimate concern for a migration file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The new spec still expects a synchronous TopicRetriever call even though the controller now enqueues a job, so it fails without covering the async contract

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the controller at app/controllers/embed_controller.rb lines 13-15 shows that when no topic_id is found, it enqueues a job: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. However, the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb lines 43-48 expects `TopicRetriever.new` to be called directly and `retriever.retrieve` to be invoked synchronously. The test mocks `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, but the actual controller code calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` instead. This means the test expectations don't match the actual implementation - the test would fail because TopicRetriever is never directly instantiated in the controller; it's only used inside the job. This is a real bug where the test doesn't properly cover the async behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:16 — Hashing after appending the localized footer couples source-change detection to presentation text, so footer or locale changes trigger needless post revisions

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 12-16, the code appends a localized footer to contents before computing content_sha1 on line 17. This means if the locale text changes (I18n.t('embed.imported_from')), the SHA1 will differ even though the actual source content hasn't changed, triggering unnecessary post revisions. The finding correctly identifies this as a design flaw where presentation text is coupled with source-change detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — import mutates its caller-owned contents string with <<, so reusing the input can accumulate duplicate imported-from footers

adjudication.rationale:
Looking at the diff for app/models/topic_embed.rb, line 13 shows `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The `<<` operator mutates the string in place. If the caller passes a string and later reuses it (or calls import multiple times with the same contents variable), the imported-from footer would accumulate. This is a real bug - the method should use `contents + "..."` or `contents.dup << "..."` to avoid mutating the caller's string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key and its Digest dependency are never used, leaving a dead cache-key abstraction with no effect on polling

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `feed_key` method is defined in poll_feed.rb (lines 20-22) but is never called anywhere in the diff. This creates dead code - a method with a Digest dependency that serves no purpose. While not a bug (the code still functions), this is a legitimate code quality issue that a reviewer should flag - unused code should be removed or the intended caching mechanism should be implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every missing embed enqueues a job before the worker-side throttle runs, so a cold-request burst can flood Sidekiq with duplicate retrieval jobs.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. In embed_controller.rb:15, when no topic_id is found, the code immediately enqueues a RetrieveTopic job via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The throttling logic exists in TopicRetriever (lib/topic_retriever.rb) via `retrieved_recently?` which uses Redis setnx, but this check happens inside the job's `perform_retrieve` method, not before the job is enqueued. This means multiple concurrent requests for the same missing embed URL will each enqueue separate Sidekiq jobs before any throttling occurs. The first job to run will set the Redis key, but the jobs are already queued. This is a real race condition that could flood Sidekiq with duplicate jobs during a burst of requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — The poller downloads and parses the entire feed without a byte or item limit, so an oversized or growing feed can exhaust worker memory on every poll.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that poll_feed.rb at line 29 uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` which downloads the entire feed without any size limits. This is a legitimate concern - if the feed URL points to a very large file, it could consume excessive memory. However, this is more of a robustness/defensive coding concern rather than a bug, since it would only manifest with malicious or misconfigured feed URLs. The code does work correctly for normal RSS feeds. This is a valid architectural concern about the new code but not a defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — Iterating every feed item calls an import that performs a separate embed lookup, creating an unbounded N+1 database workload for large feeds.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that poll_feed.rb iterates over rss.items and calls TopicEmbed.import for each item (lines 28-34). Looking at TopicEmbed.import in the diff, it performs 'TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first' for each call, which is indeed an N+1 pattern - one query per feed item. However, this is a design/performance concern rather than a bug - the code will function correctly, just inefficiently for large feeds. The finding is accurate and grounded in the diff, pointing to a real architectural issue with the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Reading the entire remote article into one String before Readability parsing lets a large valid response exhaust a worker's memory.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, `open(url).read` reads the entire remote content into memory before passing to Readability::Document. This is visible in the diff: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`. A malicious or large valid response could exhaust worker memory. This is a real security/resource exhaustion concern introduced by this new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Every distinct missing embed reruns the complete feed download and per-item import instead of reusing the scheduled poll result, multiplying remote and database work.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 38-42, when perform_retrieve is called and the embed doesn't exist, it calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) which downloads and processes the entire RSS feed. This happens for every distinct missing embed URL that triggers a retrieval. While this is technically correct behavior (it checks if the embed exists after polling), it does represent inefficient design where multiple concurrent requests for different missing embeds would each trigger a full feed poll. This is a valid architectural/efficiency concern about the new code, though not a bug since the code functions correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — The throttle is recorded before retrieval succeeds, so a Sidekiq retry within 60 seconds exits successfully without retrying the failed fetch.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb, the `retrieved_recently?` method sets a Redis key with 60-second expiry using `setnx` before any retrieval is attempted. The `retrieve` method calls `retrieved_recently?` first, and only if it returns false does it proceed to `perform_retrieve`. If `perform_retrieve` fails (e.g., network error), the Redis key is already set, so any retry within 60 seconds will have `retrieved_recently?` return true, causing the retry to exit early without actually retrying the fetch. This is a real bug in the throttling logic - the throttle should only be recorded after successful retrieval, not before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Any feed download or parsing exception aborts the on-demand retriever before its direct HTTP fallback, making a broken optional feed disable all new embeds.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 35-45, the perform_retrieve method calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) when feed_polling_enabled? is true. Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the poll_feed method uses SimpleRSS.parse and open() which can throw exceptions (network errors, parsing errors, etc.). If an exception occurs during feed polling, it will propagate up and abort perform_retrieve before reaching the fetch_http fallback on line 49. This means a broken RSS feed configuration would prevent the direct HTTP import from ever being attempted, which is a real bug in the error handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — Disabling retries causes a transient network, parser, or database error to abandon the entire feed run until the next hourly schedule.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `sidekiq_options retry: false` on line 12 of poll_feed.rb. This is a real architectural concern - disabling retries means any transient failure (network timeout, temporary database issue, RSS parsing error) will cause the job to fail silently without retry until the next hourly schedule. This is a legitimate design concern about the new code's resilience, though it's not strictly a bug since the behavior is intentional. The finding correctly identifies specific code in the diff and raises a valid operational concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — A feed item without content raises on `scrub` and aborts every later item instead of skipping or falling back to its description.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35, the code is `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item has nil content (i.content is nil), calling .scrub on nil will raise a NoMethodError, which would abort processing of all subsequent items in the feed. This is a real bug - RSS/ATOM feeds can have items without content (only title/link), and the code doesn't handle this case with a fallback to description or by skipping the item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8 — Permanent retrieval failures reload and enqueue forever because the loading state has no attempt limit or terminal error path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the loading.html.erb view. Looking at the diff, the loading page (lines 1-12 of app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) sets up a 30-second auto-reload with no termination condition. When embed#best cannot find a topic_id, it enqueues a RetrieveTopic job and renders 'loading'. If the retrieval permanently fails (e.g., invalid URL, unreachable host, parsing error), the page will keep reloading every 30 seconds indefinitely, continuously enqueuing new jobs. The TopicRetriever has throttling (60 seconds) but no permanent failure tracking. This creates an infinite loop scenario for permanently failing URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Reading an arbitrary remote article to EOF without an end-to-end deadline or response-size limit can monopolize or exhaust a background worker.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to line 48 in topic_embed.rb where `open(url).read` is called without any timeout, size limit, or deadline. Looking at the diff, the `import_remote` method does indeed call `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` which reads the entire response from an arbitrary remote URL. This is a real security/reliability concern - a malicious or slow server could cause the worker to hang indefinitely or exhaust memory with a very large response. This is a verifiable defect in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Reading the configured feed without an end-to-end deadline or response-size limit can monopolize or exhaust the scheduled worker.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows line 27 in poll_feed.rb uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` to fetch an RSS feed without any timeout, size limit, or deadline. This is a real security/reliability issue - a malicious or slow feed URL could cause the scheduled worker to hang indefinitely or consume excessive memory. The code directly opens a user-configured URL in a background job without protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Untrusted feed contents are stored as raw HTML with validation disabled, enabling persistent XSS in forum and embed views.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. Looking at post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any sanitization. The content comes from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb) or remote URLs (import_remote) and is stored/rendered as raw HTML. While ruby-readability does some tag filtering, the RSS feed path in poll_feed.rb uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` which doesn't sanitize for XSS. This creates a persistent XSS vulnerability where malicious content in feeds could execute JavaScript in users' browsers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The server fetches the user-selected URL without revalidating scheme, port, redirects, or resolved addresses, enabling SSRF through the allowed host.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real SSRF vulnerability in the new code at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48. The `import_remote` method uses `open(url).read` where the URL comes from user input (via embed_url parameter or RSS feed). While `import` method at line 10 checks for `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, the `import_remote` method at line 48 directly opens the URL without validating the resolved IP address, following redirects, or checking for internal network addresses. An attacker could potentially use this to access internal services by providing URLs that resolve to internal IPs or through redirect chains. This is a legitimate security concern in the newly added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — A forgeable Referer header is the only gate on a public endpoint that enqueues topic creation as the configured embed user.
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same core security concern as the golden comment - that the referer header validation is the only protection mechanism and can be easily bypassed/forged. Both comments point to the referer validation being insufficient security. The golden comment also mentions X-Frame-Options and the nil referer fallback, which the candidate doesn't mention, but the primary security issue (forgeable referer header as the only gate) is the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — The no-embed example asserts a mocked downstream TopicRetriever rather than that :retrieve_topic is enqueued with the embed URL and user, so the controller/job contract is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 mocks TopicRetriever and verifies that retrieve is called on the mock, but doesn't verify that Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) is called with the correct parameters. Looking at the controller code in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14, when no topic_id is found, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)`. The test mocks TopicRetriever directly rather than verifying the job is enqueued properly, so the contract between the controller and the job system is not tested. This is a valid test coverage concern for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:31 — Success coverage always reuses the referer as embed_url, missing that an existing cross-host embed bypasses TopicRetriever host validation and is rendered.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a security issue where 'an existing cross-host embed bypasses TopicRetriever host validation'. Looking at the diff, when a topic_id is found via TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(), it renders the topic directly without going through TopicRetriever. However, the ensure_embeddable filter in EmbedController still validates that the referer host matches SiteSetting.embeddable_host before any rendering occurs. The TopicEmbed records are created through controlled import processes (RSS polling or TopicRetriever), not arbitrary cross-host URLs. The test coverage concern about 'reusing referer as embed_url' is not a real security bypass - the referer validation in ensure_embeddable is the security gate, not the embed_url parameter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — Both valid-host examples stub perform_retrieve or retrieved_recently?, leaving the Redis throttle, existing-embed, feed-first, and HTTP-fallback behavior completely unexecuted.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test file spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb stubs out key methods (perform_retrieve and retrieved_recently?) in the 'with a valid host' context, which means the actual implementation logic in perform_retrieve (Redis throttle, existing-embed check, feed-first logic, HTTP-fallback via fetch_http) is never exercised by these tests. Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve contains significant logic including checking TopicEmbed.exists?, conditionally running Jobs::PollFeed, and calling fetch_http - none of which gets tested. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:21 — URL validation coverage only uses an unparsable string and misses syntactically valid non-HTTP URLs such as ftp URLs, which the current validation accepts and fetches.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a gap in test coverage. Looking at the diff, the test in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:21 tests 'not a url' which is unparsable. However, the actual validation in lib/topic_retriever.rb only checks if the host matches embeddable_host - it doesn't validate the URL scheme. The TopicEmbed.import method (line 10-11) does check for http/https URLs with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, but TopicRetriever.fetch_http calls TopicEmbed.import_remote which uses `open(url)` without scheme validation. This is a legitimate test coverage gap - the test doesn't cover syntactically valid non-HTTP URLs like ftp:// that would pass URI parsing but shouldn't be fetched.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:31 — The enabled-path spec mocks poll_feed itself, so feed parsing, link-to-id fallback, content handling, and TopicEmbed imports receive no behavioral coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests that poll_feed is called when conditions are met (line 31-37), but mocks the poll_feed method itself with `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`. This means the actual feed parsing logic in poll_feed (lines 23-36 of app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) including SimpleRSS parsing, link/id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, and TopicEmbed.import calls are not tested. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:33 — The relative-URL example covers only root-relative paths, missing document-relative and protocol-relative href or src values that absolutize_urls currently leaves unresolved.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a gap in test coverage. Looking at the diff, the `absolutize_urls` method in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` only handles URLs that `start_with?('/')` (root-relative paths). The test in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` uses `` and `` which are both root-relative. The finding correctly notes that document-relative URLs (like `href='hello'` without leading slash) and protocol-relative URLs (like `//example.com/image.jpg`) would not be converted by the current implementation. This is a valid observation about incomplete edge-case handling in both the implementation and tests, though it's more of a missing feature than a bug since the code does what it explicitly checks for.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The new skip_validations save branch has no differentiating test because the only update example revises an already-valid post.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that lib/post_revisor.rb line 85 adds a new code path with `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` that allows skipping validations when the option is passed. Looking at the diff, this new skip_validations option is used in topic_embed.rb line 35 with `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)`. However, the test file spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only tests the 'Supports updating the post' scenario with a simple content change on an already-valid post, not specifically testing the skip_validations behavior. This is a legitimate observation about missing test coverage for a new code path, though the severity is moderate since the feature does work (as shown by the import test passing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — No client test covers near-match message origins, so the substring-based postMessage origin check can accept a different origin without detection.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security issue in the embed.js code at line 16-17: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This substring check using indexOf is insecure because an attacker could register a domain like 'eviltrout.com.attacker.com' which would pass the check if discourseUrl is 'eviltrout.com'. The correct approach would be to use strict equality or proper URL parsing. This is a verifiable security defect in the new code being added.
